course.title: SQL Masterclass
course.tagline: Zero to advanced, one module at a time.
course.standard: PostgreSQL-first, with MySQL, SQLite and SQL Server notes.
course.description: Module 06 teaches SELECT from the basic projection to aliases, calculated columns, concatenation, DISTINCT and the logical order of query evaluation.

modules.title: SELECT Statement
modules.goal: Read and shape result sets with correct projection and expressions.

topics.title: Introduction to SELECT
topics.simple: SELECT database se data padhne ka command hai — jo columns chahiye, wo choose karta hai.
topics.pro: SELECT is DQL that projects a result set from one or more relations, evaluates expressions and returns rows without modifying stored data.
points: It can return zero, one or many rows.
The result columns are defined by the select list.

example.sql: SELECT name, marks FROM students;
example.output: One row per student with name and marks.

topics.title: Basic SELECT Syntax
topics.simple: Basic shape: SELECT columns FROM table.
topics.pro: The core syntax is SELECT select_list FROM relation [WHERE ...] [ORDER BY ...] [LIMIT ...]; the select list defines the output columns.

example.sql: SELECT id, name FROM students;

topics.title: SELECT *
topics.simple: SELECT * table ke saare columns deta hai.
topics.pro: SELECT * expands to every column in the relation at planning time; it is convenient for exploration but fragile in production.
points: It returns every column, including future ones.
Column order follows the table definition.

example.sql: SELECT * FROM students;
example.output: Every column and row from students.

topics.title: Selecting Specific Columns
topics.simple: Sirf zaroori columns choose karo — network aur result chhota rehta hai.
topics.pro: A projection list names the columns to return; omitted columns are not read into the result, which can reduce I/O and payload.
points: The output order is the list order.

example.sql: SELECT name, marks FROM students;

topics.title: Selecting Multiple Columns
topics.simple: Comma se multiple columns likho.
topics.pro: Multiple columns are separated by commas and appear in the same order as the select list, regardless of table order.
points: A trailing comma is a syntax error.

example.sql: SELECT id, name, email, marks FROM students;

topics.title: Column Aliases
topics.simple: Alias result column ka temporary naam hota hai.
topics.pro: An alias renames a result column for the query output; it does not rename the underlying table column.
points: Aliases are not visible in WHERE in PostgreSQL.

example.sql: SELECT name AS student_name, marks AS score FROM students;

topics.title: AS Keyword
topics.simple: AS alias ko explicit banata hai — padhne me clear.
topics.pro: AS introduces a column or table alias; it is optional for column aliases but required for some derived-table aliases.
points: AS is optional for column aliases.
Quoted aliases preserve case and spaces.
Aliases last for the query only.

example.sql: SELECT name AS "Student Name" FROM students;

topics.title: Calculated Columns
topics.simple: SELECT me expression se naya column bana sakte hain.
topics.pro: The select list can contain expressions, not just columns; each expression becomes an output column with a computed value per row.
points: Calculations do not change stored data.
Use an alias to name the result.
The expression is evaluated per row.

example.sql: SELECT name, marks + 5 AS boosted FROM students;

topics.title: Arithmetic Operations
topics.simple: SELECT me +, -, *, /, % use kar sakte hain.
topics.pro: Arithmetic operators follow standard precedence; integer division truncates, while a numeric operand keeps the fraction.

example.sql: SELECT 7 / 2 AS int_div, ROUND(7.0 / 2, 1) AS num_div;

topics.title: Concatenating Columns
topics.simple: || operator strings ko jodta hai.
topics.pro: The || operator concatenates text; cast non-text values explicitly when the result must be predictable.
points: NULL concatenated with anything is NULL.

example.sql: SELECT name || ' scored ' || marks::text AS label FROM students;

topics.title: Selecting Expressions
topics.simple: SELECT me literals, functions aur arithmetic — sab expressions hain.
topics.pro: A select-list item can be a column, literal, function call or arithmetic expression; PostgreSQL names an unaliased expression ?column?.
points: Use aliases for stable column names.
Functions run per row unless aggregated.

example.sql: SELECT 2 + 3 * 4 AS result;

topics.title: SELECT DISTINCT
topics.simple: DISTINCT duplicate result rows hata deta hai.
topics.pro: SELECT DISTINCT removes duplicate rows from the final result after projection; it applies to the whole select list, not to one column.
points: DISTINCT is applied after SELECT expressions.
It treats NULLs as equal for duplicate removal.
It can cost a sort or hash.

example.sql: SELECT DISTINCT marks FROM students;

topics.title: Duplicate Values
topics.simple: Table me same value kai rows me ho sakti hai; DISTINCT unhe ek baar dikhata hai.
topics.pro: Duplicates are normal in relational data unless a constraint forbids them; duplicate removal is a query-time decision, not a storage rule.
points: A primary key prevents duplicate rows by key.
DISTINCT changes the result, not the table.

example.sql: SELECT marks FROM students;

topics.title: DISTINCT with Multiple Columns
topics.simple: Multiple columns ke saath DISTINCT unique combinations deta hai.
topics.pro: SELECT DISTINCT a, b removes duplicate pairs; it does not return one row per distinct a.
points: Column order does not change the set.
Use GROUP BY when you need aggregates per key.

example.sql: SELECT DISTINCT name, marks FROM students;

topics.title: Logical Query Order
topics.simple: SQL likhne ka order aur database ke evaluate karne ka order alag hai.
topics.pro: Logical evaluation is FROM → WHERE → GROUP BY → HAVING → SELECT → DISTINCT → ORDER BY → LIMIT, which explains alias visibility and filter timing.
points: Aliases are available in ORDER BY.

example.sql: SELECT name AS n FROM students ORDER BY n;
example.output: Rows sorted by the alias n.

topics.title: Understanding Query Results
topics.simple: Result ek table jaisa hota hai — columns aur rows; zero rows bhi valid result hai.
topics.pro: A SELECT result is a relation with named columns and zero or more rows; an empty result is not an error and does not mean NULL.
points: Zero rows is a valid answer.
Column names come from the select list.
NULL is a value, not an empty result.

example.sql: SELECT name FROM students WHERE marks > 100;

topics.title: SELECT Query Execution
topics.simple: Database query ko parse, plan aur execute karta hai.
topics.pro: The server parses the statement, rewrites it, plans access paths, then executes; EXPLAIN shows the plan without running the query.
points: The planner chooses scans and joins.

example.sql: EXPLAIN SELECT * FROM students WHERE id = 1;

topics.title: Common SELECT Mistakes
topics.simple: Common galtiyan: galat column, missing comma, alias WHERE me use karna, integer division bhoolna.
topics.pro: Typical mistakes are misspelled columns, trailing commas, assuming alias visibility in WHERE, integer division and expecting DISTINCT to apply to one column.

example.sql: SELECT names FROM students;

topics.title: SELECT Without FROM
topics.simple: PostgreSQL me FROM ke bina bhi expression select kar sakte hain.
topics.pro: SELECT without FROM evaluates the select list once and returns one row; it is useful for testing expressions and functions.
points: No table means one synthetic row.

example.sql: SELECT 1 + 1 AS answer;

topics.title: Practical Student Report Query
topics.simple: Ab columns, alias, calculation aur concatenation mila kar report banao.
topics.pro: A report query combines projection, aliases and expressions to produce a readable result without changing the table.

example.sql: SELECT id, name AS student, marks, marks + 5 AS boosted, name || ' (' || marks::text || ')' AS label FROM students;
example.output: A table with id, student, marks, boosted and label columns.

learn.q: Which category does SELECT belong to?
learn.why: SELECT reads data; many curricula call that DQL.

learn.q: What does SELECT * return?
learn.why: * expands to every column at planning time.

learn.q: How do you return only name and marks?
learn.why: List the columns in the select list.

learn.q: Which keyword gives a result column a temporary name?
learn.why: AS introduces a column alias.

learn.q: Is AS required for a column alias?
learn.why: SELECT name n is a valid alias form.

learn.q: What does SELECT 7 / 2 return?
learn.why: Both operands are integers, so integer division truncates.

learn.q: What does ROUND(7.0 / 2, 1) return?
learn.why: 7.0 is numeric, so the division keeps the fraction, and ROUND fixes the display scale.

learn.q: Which operator concatenates text?
learn.why: PostgreSQL uses || for string concatenation.

learn.q: What does SELECT DISTINCT do?
learn.why: DISTINCT removes duplicate projected rows.

learn.q: Does DISTINCT apply to one column or the whole select list?
learn.why: The entire projected tuple is compared.

learn.q: Which clause runs first logically?
learn.why: The source rows are established before projection.

learn.q: Can a column alias be used in WHERE in PostgreSQL?
learn.why: WHERE is evaluated before SELECT, so the alias does not exist yet.

learn.q: Can a column alias be used in ORDER BY?
learn.why: ORDER BY is evaluated after SELECT, so aliases are available.

learn.q: Is SELECT 1; valid in PostgreSQL?
learn.why: SELECT without FROM evaluates the expression once.

learn.q: What is an unaliased expression column named?
learn.why: PostgreSQL uses ?column? when no alias is given.

learn.q: What does SELECT NULL return?
learn.why: NULL is a value, not an empty result.

learn.q: How many columns does SELECT name FROM students return?
learn.why: The select list has one item.

learn.q: What does SELECT 2 + 3 * 4 return?
learn.why: Multiplication binds tighter than addition.

learn.q: What does SELECT (2 + 3) * 4 return?
learn.why: Parentheses force the addition first.

learn.q: What does a SELECT returning zero rows mean?
learn.why: No matching rows is a normal result set.

interview.q: What is SELECT?
interview.answer: DQL that projects a result set from relations and expressions without changing stored rows.

interview.q: What is the basic SELECT syntax?
interview.answer: SELECT select_list FROM relation [WHERE ...] [ORDER BY ...] [LIMIT ...];

interview.q: What is the logical order of query evaluation?
interview.answer: FROM, WHERE, GROUP BY, HAVING, SELECT, DISTINCT, ORDER BY, LIMIT.

interview.q: Why is SELECT * risky in production?
interview.answer: It returns every current and future column, can break consumers and transfers more data than needed.

interview.q: What is a column alias?
interview.answer: A temporary name for a result column; it does not rename the table column.

interview.q: Is AS required for an alias?
interview.answer: No, it is optional for column aliases, but it improves clarity.

interview.q: How do you preserve spaces or case in an alias?
interview.answer: Double-quote it, for example AS "Student Name".

interview.q: What is the difference between DISTINCT and GROUP BY?
interview.answer: DISTINCT removes duplicate projected rows; GROUP BY forms groups for aggregates and can be paired with HAVING.

interview.q: Does DISTINCT apply to one column or all selected columns?
interview.answer: All selected columns; the whole tuple is compared.

interview.q: How does DISTINCT treat NULL?
interview.answer: It treats NULLs as equal for duplicate removal, so one NULL survives.

interview.q: Why does 7 / 2 return 3?
interview.answer: Both operands are integers, so integer division truncates the fraction.

interview.q: How do you get 3.5 from 7 and 2?
interview.answer: Use a numeric operand and round the display, for example ROUND(7.0 / 2, 1). A bare numeric division can display extra scale digits.

interview.q: What does || do with NULL?
interview.answer: Concatenating NULL with anything returns NULL; use COALESCE if a fallback is needed.

interview.q: Why is an unaliased expression column called ?column??
interview.answer: PostgreSQL needs a name; without an alias it uses ?column? for the expression.

interview.q: Can SELECT run without FROM?
interview.answer: Yes. It evaluates the select list once and returns one row.

interview.q: Is SELECT read-only?
interview.answer: It does not change stored rows, though it can call functions; it is DQL.

interview.q: Why are aliases unavailable in WHERE?
interview.answer: Logical evaluation runs WHERE before SELECT, so the alias has not been defined yet.

interview.q: Why are aliases available in ORDER BY?
interview.answer: ORDER BY runs after SELECT, so the projected alias exists.

interview.q: What does an empty result set mean?
interview.answer: The query matched zero rows; it is not an error and not a NULL row.

interview.q: What is the difference between a column and an expression in SELECT?
interview.answer: A column reads a stored value; an expression computes a new value per row.

labs.title: Select every column
labs.task: Return every column and row from students.

labs.title: Select two columns
labs.expected: name and marks for every student.

labs.title: Alias a column
labs.solution: SELECT name AS student_name FROM students;

labs.title: Alias without AS
labs.task: Return marks as score without the AS keyword.

labs.title: Calculate a column
labs.task: Return name and marks plus 5 as boosted.
labs.solution: SELECT name, marks + 5 AS boosted FROM students;
labs.expected: boosted is five higher than marks.

labs.title: Numeric division
labs.task: Return 7.0 / 2 rounded to one decimal as num_div.

labs.title: Concatenate a label
labs.task: Return name and marks as a label.
labs.solution: SELECT name || ' scored ' || marks::text AS label FROM students;

labs.title: Select a literal
labs.task: Return the text ready as status.

labs.title: Distinct pairs
labs.task: Return each unique name and marks pair.
labs.solution: SELECT DISTINCT name, marks FROM students;

labs.title: Quoted alias
labs.solution: SELECT name AS "Student Name" FROM students;
labs.expected: A column with the exact header Student Name.

labs.title: Filtered select
labs.task: Return name and marks for students above 80.
labs.solution: SELECT name, marks FROM students WHERE marks > 80;

labs.title: Count rows
labs.solution: SELECT COUNT(*) AS total FROM students;

labs.title: Build a report row
labs.task: Return id, name, marks, marks plus 5 and a label.
labs.solution: SELECT id, name AS student, marks, marks + 5 AS boosted, name || ' (' || marks::text || ')' AS label FROM students;

logic.q: Why can an alias not be used in WHERE?
logic.answer: WHERE is evaluated before SELECT, so the alias has not been defined yet.

logic.q: Why is an alias available in ORDER BY?
logic.answer: ORDER BY is evaluated after SELECT, so the projected alias exists.

logic.q: Why does DISTINCT apply to the whole select list?
logic.answer: It compares complete projected rows; there is no per-column mode.

logic.q: Why can SELECT * break an application?
logic.answer: A new column changes the result shape and can break consumers that expect a fixed set.
Both operands are integers, so integer division truncates.
7.0 is numeric, so the division uses numeric arithmetic.

logic.q: Why does NULL || text return NULL?
logic.answer: Concatenation with an unknown value is unknown; use COALESCE to supply a default.

logic.q: Why does multiplication run before addition?
logic.answer: SQL arithmetic gives * and / higher precedence than + and -.

logic.q: Why do parentheses matter in expressions?
logic.answer: They override precedence and make the intended grouping explicit.

logic.q: Why is an unaliased expression called ?column??
logic.answer: The result needs a name; PostgreSQL supplies a placeholder when none is given.

logic.q: Why is SELECT without FROM useful?
logic.answer: It evaluates expressions and functions once without needing a table.
It may sort or hash the whole result to find duplicates.

logic.q: Why does a zero-row result not mean NULL?
logic.answer: Zero rows is an empty relation; NULL is a value inside a row.

logic.q: Why quote an alias with spaces?
logic.answer: Unquoted identifiers cannot contain spaces and fold to lowercase; quotes preserve the exact text.
The parser normalizes keywords, so SELECT and select mean the same thing.

debug.title: Alias in WHERE
debug.broken: SELECT name AS n FROM students WHERE n = 'Aarav';
debug.fix: SELECT name AS n FROM students WHERE name = 'Aarav';

debug.title: DISTINCT misconception
debug.broken: SELECT DISTINCT name, marks FROM students;
debug.error: Returns unique pairs, not unique names

debug.title: Missing expression
debug.fix: SELECT name, marks + 5 AS boosted FROM students;

debug.title: Order by missing position
debug.broken: SELECT name, marks FROM students ORDER BY 3;
debug.fix: SELECT name, marks FROM students ORDER BY marks;
debug.error: ORDER BY position 3 is not in select list

debug.title: Unquoted alias with spaces
debug.broken: SELECT name AS Student Name FROM students;
debug.fix: SELECT name AS "Student Name" FROM students;

debug.title: Empty result is not NULL
debug.broken: SELECT name FROM students WHERE marks > 100;
debug.fix: SELECT COALESCE((SELECT name FROM students WHERE marks > 100 LIMIT 1), 'none') AS name;
debug.error: Returns zero rows, not a NULL row

revision.answer: Projects a result set from relations and expressions without changing stored rows.

revision.q: How do you alias a column?

revision.answer: Removes duplicate result rows across the whole select list.

revision.q: How do you keep a fraction?
revision.answer: Use a numeric operand, such as 7.0 / 2.

revision.q: What is the logical order of evaluation?
revision.answer: FROM, WHERE, GROUP BY, HAVING, SELECT, DISTINCT, ORDER BY, LIMIT.

revision.q: What does a zero-row result mean?
revision.answer: The query matched no rows; it is a valid empty result.
